claim: Pointing states are independent (convolution valid)
test: Exact CDF vs time-percentile CDF of the scan clock, 74 modes, 5 trials of 1800 s, 0/0 deg
criterion: Exact value inside the time-series 95% interval (allowing the exact bias) for every mode
key_result: 2 of 296 mode-percentile checks outside the 95% interval (50%: 0, 90%: 0, 99%: 0, 99.9%: 2). Largest |ts - exact| 1.02 dB.

claim: The ATC rate tolerance does not matter
test: Fixed ATC rates across 74.5 to 75.5 deg/s (0.025 deg/s step), time series vs exact CDF, worst three modes
criterion: No rate where clock and exact CDFs differ by more than 1 dB at 99.9%
key_result: 41 rates x 3 modes x 2 trials of 3600 s. Largest |deviation| at 99.9%: 0.40 dB (VCP 12 SAILSx3 AVSET 6.4, CD 12.524, 74.825 deg/s); 0 runs over 1 dB.

claim: The envelope bounds any mix of modes
test: Random mode mixtures (Dirichlet, 5,000) and every mid-volume mode change (cuts 1..s of X, then Y), 0/0 deg
criterion: Mixture bound holds; transitions add no exceedance above the envelope
key_result: Mixtures: largest exceedance above the envelope 0 (round-off). Mode change mid-volume, window of the partial volume plus the next: up to 1.35/0.65/0.00 dB above the envelope at 99/99.9/99.99%.
next_step: The envelope bounds every mixture of whole volumes (proof: the mixture exceedance is a weighted mean of mode exceedances). A volume cut short by a mode change repeats the low cuts, so that window can exceed the envelope; it lasts one volume, so the long-run CDF moves little. State it in the report; per-volume harm (D4) is the metric that sees it.
